summary:
Hauts-de-France legislates nothing of its own on detention, identity documents or anti-discrimination. The region stands under the national framework of France: custodial placement, gender markers and discrimination protections are set nationally. No regional statute, regional court ruling or regional administrative instruction on transgender detainees or visitors appears in the sources.

The single documented case in the region is Paola, a trans woman whose identity documents record her as male, transferred in 2014 to the correctional facility at Lille and held in a men's establishment. Detainees there shouted "We don't want any women here!"; a fellow inmate tried to attack her with a knife; she spent two days in solitary confinement. The account was published in a BuzzFeed News investigation of 12 January 2018.
tangentialFactors: The national detention-oversight authority's remit covers every place of deprivation of liberty in France, including establishments in Hauts-de-France; the region has no prison inspectorate, human-rights body or equality body of its own, so custody oversight and discrimination complaints run through national institutions. The region's one documented custodial case sits inside a pattern described nationally; nothing in the sources marks Hauts-de-France as better or worse than other regions, and no comparison or ranking between regions exists.
localsOnly: Trans residents of Hauts-de-France held in custody are placed under nationally set rules; the region runs no separate placement policy, no regional gender-recognition procedure and no regional anti-discrimination mechanism. Complaints about custodial treatment, or about discrimination in services and employment, are handled by national institutions rather than by any regional body.
outOfScopeNotes: No regional breakdown of the national count of transgender detainees is available, so the number held in Hauts-de-France facilities is not sourced. No statistics for the region on violence, discrimination or enforcement were identified, and no region-specific material on border or entry screening was found. The Lille case rests on a single account published in 2018 about events in 2014; no follow-up reporting on Paola's situation or on conditions at that facility is in the sources.
